technical_hypothesis.interaction_pattern: batch or online human-in-the-loop policy evaluation
technical_hypothesis.primary_training_data_risk: historical actions were selected by engineers under severity, ownership, customer, release, workload and staffing conditions that are incompletely recorded, while alternative eligible interventions and assignment propensities are usually absent

training_data.observation_unit: a workload optimization decision, release rollout decision or incident-recovery decision at a defined decision point
training_data.input_data: confirmed candidate inputs include pre-decision service telemetry, cost and usage, release metadata, incident context, ownership, customer impact and eligible-action constraints; customer-specific completeness is unknown
training_data.target_or_reward: incremental change in cost, reliability, incident rate, recovery time, recurrence, user outcome or delivery delay attributable to one bounded intervention rather than another
training_data.label_source: post-decision telemetry, cost records, incident outcomes, rollback events, support resolution and recurrence; causal validity of these outcomes is unknown
training_data.prediction_time: after deterministic eligibility, safety, permission and SLO checks and before an intervention is selected
training_data.expected_volume: unknown and likely fragmented across teams, products, clouds and intervention types
training_data.class_balance: not directly applicable as a simple class ratio; treatment groups and rare adverse outcomes are expected to be uneven
training_data.historical_coverage: unknown; most operational systems record the chosen action and result but not all eligible alternatives, assignment rationale or probability
training_data.train_validation_split: time-based and service or product-grouped evaluation would be required, with prospective holdouts or randomized rollout where safe
training_data.leakage_risks: using post-intervention telemetry, final incident severity, rollback decisions, resolved root cause, later ownership corrections or cost outcomes unavailable at decision time
training_data.representativeness_risks: service architecture, customer mix, cloud pricing, release process, team maturity, traffic shape and intervention policy vary materially across products and periods
training_data.feedback_loop: recommendations change which interventions are observed, potentially eliminating counterfactual coverage and reinforcing incumbent engineering choices
training_data.privacy_and_usage_constraints: tenant support data, telemetry and developer or operator activity must be minimized and governed under LGPD and internal employment, security and confidentiality controls
training_data.fallback_if_data_is_insufficient: use feature flags, controlled canaries, deterministic rollback and SLO gates, FinOps policy-as-code, native cost recommendations, explicit experiment design and human review; instrument treatment eligibility and assignment prospectively before causal modeling

portfolio_comparison.reason: The simulated questions are genuinely causal, but current workflows lack trustworthy treatment assignment and counterfactual coverage. Progressive delivery, feature flags, controlled experiments, deterministic SLO gates, FinOps policy-as-code and existing optimization recommendations already provide safer decision mechanisms. A causal model would be an internal analytical capability after prospective instrumentation, not a differentiated repository opportunity today.

existing_landscape.summary: Adopt controlled experimentation, feature flags, progressive exposure, deterministic rollback and FinOps governance. Instrument eligible actions, assignment rationale, propensity and outcomes prospectively; reconsider causal estimation only after sufficient comparable interventions exist.

research.findings: Brazilian public-service incidents and current FinOps material confirm that reliability and cloud-value decisions remain operationally relevant. Current feature-flag and experimentation platforms already support progressive exposure, rollback and controlled measurement. Recent causal-software-engineering research frames causal reasoning as promising but still emphasizes explicit assumptions, confounding control and an evaluation roadmap rather than a mature default operational capability.
